🗓 **TAWG Daily Catch-up**
_2026-10-12 23:00 → 2026-10-13 23:00 UTC_

## ⚡ **Highlights**

> **Mode 3 handoff loop closed** — A binding-check concern proved genuinely load-bearing, the contract was hardened and frozen, and a teammate queued the artifact for immediate review. [tg:tawg:5482]

> **Recompute-kit runtime gating validated** — Cross-contributor fixture testing confirmed isolation as the correct enforcement mechanism, completing a full ship-and-validate cycle for the dependency gate. [tg:tawg:5465]

> **Empirical data joined the ERC-8004 forum** — Production measurements from Base on trust-feature adoption gave the spec discussion a concrete real-world anchor. [ERC-8004 post](https://ethereum-magicians.org/t/erc-8004-trustless-agents/25098/415)

## 🤝 **What moved**

### re4ctor

_Mode 3 moved from an open concern to a verified, frozen artifact ready for review._

- Pavlo (@pavlentyy82) **Validated** that the binding-check gap was genuinely load-bearing by prototyping and cold-testing the contract, catching a potential silent regression before it could reach the handoff package. [tg:tawg:5461]
- Pavlo (@pavlentyy82) **Continued** an independent XRPL adapter PoC that originated around a hackathon context, keeping the adapter work moving forward even after in-person participation was no longer possible. [tg:tawg:5462]
- Pavlo (@pavlentyy82) **Packaged** the frozen Mode 3 handoff artifact with a published SHA-256, giving reviewers a verifiable baseline and formally closing the open handoff action. [tg:tawg:5482]
- Merlini (@gobross) **Picked up** the handoff zip immediately after delivery, committing to run it right away and keeping the review loop tight so the artifact does not sit idle. [tg:tawg:5484]

### recompute-kit

_The runtime dependency gate completed a full ship-and-validate cycle across two contributors._

- Baby Blue Viper **Shipped** recompute-kit #69, adding runtime dependency declarations to suite.json for commands, node packages, and Python modules so the runner can gate execution before any adapter fires and close a class of silent environment failures. [tg:tawg:5458]
- Zexo (@zexoverz) **Confirmed** the isolation mechanism by running fixup fixtures cold against #68 and finding that a same-size pair returns KILLED—a precise result that validates the approach and surfaces a specific edge case for the next iteration. [tg:tawg:5465]
- Baby Blue Viper **Clarified** how the merged runtime.commands declaration interacts with direct gate.py invocations, identifying a bypass path that would silently skip the dependency gate if not addressed. [tg:tawg:5477]

### zkIE

_Shard boundary proof design is in active exploration._

- Jimmy Shi (@jimmyshi) **Synced** the group on zkIE progress, explaining the goal of avoiding full replay on every proof verification and the open question of whether to keep WHIR or move to an alternative—keeping the group oriented on where the design space remains unsettled. [tg:tawg:5464]

### ERC-8004

_Real-world usage data arrived to complement the spec discussion._

- Measurements from Base on how trust features are used in production were shared on the forum, providing an empirical grounding for the ERC-8004 discussion and connecting normative design choices to observed deployment patterns. [ERC-8004 post](https://ethereum-magicians.org/t/erc-8004-trustless-agents/25098/415)

### ERC-8312

_A concrete reservation design question surfaced in the forum._

- A question posted to the ERC-8312 thread on whether agent order amendments should resize a single reservation or track deltas through separate reservations opens a precise design choice affecting how bounded-action agents handle partial fills. [ERC-8312 post](https://ethereum-magicians.org/t/erc-8312-bounded-agent-actions/28851/75)

## 🚀 **Next up**

### 💡 **Ideas to follow**

- The KILLED result on same-size pair testing may point to an edge case worth isolating before the next recompute-kit suite iteration
- The ERC-8312 delta-vs-resize question could benefit from a worked example to surface tradeoffs concretely
- The Base trust-feature measurements could be examined alongside ERC-8004 normative requirements for alignment signals

### ✅ **TODOs**

- Merlini to run the Mode 3 handoff artifact and share results with the group
- Investigate whether a guard is needed at the gate.py call site to prevent the runtime gate bypass
- Jimmy Shi to share a design update once the WHIR question is resolved

## 🤖 **Trusty's take**

> **Today's spark:** A concern about a single missing binding check was raised, tested, confirmed load-bearing, fixed, and sealed into a verifiable artifact with a published hash—before anyone had to ask for proof.
>
> When the loop closes that fast, the whole system is working together. Keep sealing things with hashes. 🔒
